baseline.worktree: Already contained uncommitted pass 09 implementation, tests, documentation and evidence; not a clean release baseline
baseline.publication: No version change, commit, tag, push or deployment.

scope.meaning: Authenticated history, JSON/CSV export and unread read honesty across query validation, warm/cold memory, configured storage failure/repair, cancellation/timeouts and prior fallback.
scope.boundaries: Actual Axum HTTP router with synthetic owner sessions and EventBus injected with disposable PostgreSQL 16.15; private Unix socket, DATABASE_URL unset; other services stay in-memory.
excluded: live Engine/Agent, SSH/LAN or kernel mutation
new routes/access tiers/Event/database schema/SDK signature/frontend product changes

findings.summary: Configured SQL read failures were masked by partial/empty/zero success and could disable persistence; wait and pre-existing fallback boundaries were not authoritative.
findings.fix: New fallible HTTP read path returns generic no-store 503, never an attachment on failed export; ten-second cooperative read wait includes schema/pool work and does not latch persistence off. Invalid configured and previously latched stores are not explicit memory-only mode.

findings.summary: Invalid/unknown filters, unsupported formats and overflowing relative windows could widen queries, alter format or panic.
findings.fix: Validate query extraction, filters, RFC3339 dates, export format and checked/frozen time windows before storage; no-store 400 for invalid/reversed ranges. Preserve successful shapes, session owner, inclusive timestamps, zero window, limits and legacy ignored fields.

findings.summary: Incompatible payload types fabricated empty objects and timestamp decoding panicked; initial fixes exposed cached SELECT result-type errors after column repair.
findings.fix: Fallible row decoding with generic unavailable responses; nonpersistent history SELECT prepared statements allow retry after column-type repair. Planning reuse changed without a benchmark.

tdd.authoring_note: Initial HTTP assertion incorrectly assumed 100,000,000,000 minutes overflows Chrono; corrected to 1,000,000,000,000 for date overflow, alongside i64::MAX duration overflow. Both logs retained; mistaken assertion is not a defect or an exhaustive PostgreSQL date-domain test.

repair_diagnostic.finding: cached plan must not change result type after restoring JSONB; temporary tracing setup removed from final tests

tdd.after_red_guards: Two service-level guards and final authentication/cancellation assertion extensions added after initial red reproductions; final gate and PostgreSQL logs validate final sources.

post_documentation_preflight.meaning: Final bilingual report and course mirrors, file length/version/OpenAPI/API/SDK contract and common/tool/formatter checks; runtime sources unchanged from full gate.

quality_gate.compatibility: OpenAPI/API/SDK generation and surface checks passed at unchanged version 0.4.0; 64 paths, 68 Engine operations, 63 SDK operations, 85 schemas
quality_gate.note: Distribution/SSH/kernel-smoke script checks use isolated tool fixtures, not deployment or privileged kernel acceptance.

event_postgres.command: env -u DATABASE_URL CYANREX_DB_FALLBACK=true CYANREX_TEST_DATABASE_URL=<explicit disposable private socket URL> cargo test --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml --locked --lib services::event_bus::tests -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1
event_postgres.note: Final auth/cancellation extensions included; independent schemas destroyed; table/column changes confined to fixtures.

contract_ci.note: 32 exact ordering-job selections plus the existing separately selected deletion case cover all 33 event PostgreSQL tests.

preservation.note: Original inventory and historical pass 01-09 reports/logs/mirrors remain byte-identical, including uncommitted pass 09 and captured whitespace.

limitations: Ten seconds bounds cooperative async read work, not auth, serialization, CPU stalls or proof of server-side query cancellation.
Read failures do not poison persistence; an independent writer can still latch existing fallback. Previously latched reads remain unavailable until fresh state, without volatile reconciliation.
Fresh EventBus against retained fixture rows is not process crash, network partition, lost commit or power-loss recovery.
No read queue barrier or snapshot/live atomicity; snapshots may trail live delivery. No multi-Engine/external-writer coordination.
Legacy infallible Rust helpers remain best-effort compatibility APIs, distinct from authoritative HTTP reads.
Existing volatile writes and mark-read/delete acknowledgement/durability are unchanged.
No exhaustive enum/corrupt-data validation, PostgreSQL date-domain validation, CSV formula/CR/spreadsheet safety, byte quotas, durable replay or exactly-once guarantees.
History SELECT planning reuse changed without a performance benchmark.
next: F34 mark-read/F35 deletion acknowledgement under selected storage failure and recovery using isolated fixtures; a successful read does not establish durable mutation success.
